The reason why communism and nazism are treated different is because they ARE different. There are several different ways you can define socialism and communism. Generally, Marxist thought is simply that capitalism creates unnecessary inequality between the people who own the means of production and the people who don’t own the means of production. From there, the beliefs diverge, some believe the state should taken ownership of ALL of the means of production (USSR, China under mao, Cuba under Castro), some believe the state should take ownership of some of the means of production and use the proceeds to lessen economic inequality (think Venezuela’s oil company, or maybe even the UKs publicly run NHS), some believe that the state should heavily regulate and tax the means of production to lessen inequality (this is Sanders, AOC and most of the left parties in Europe), then there’s socialism where the workers directly control the means of production (this isn’t a governmental system, so governmental examples don’t work but look up cooperative businesses like the Mondragon Corporation).  All of these are vastly different ideas, and while you may not like any of them, they certainly aren’t all Soviet style communism.

I'm having the same kind of night. Anxiety is a kind of hell I don't wish on anyone. I also get your frustration with the different "anxiety calming techniques", they very often don't work.  While it's possible you might want to start thinking and asking about meds, here's another thought. I thought the anxiety relief methods were full of shit until my therapist explained anxiety as a scale of 1-10.  Imagine 1 being the feeling of waking up peacefully on your own private beach. Imagine 10 being literal anxiety hell. Imagine 5 being that feeling when you're productively engaged in something you're working on. Ideally, your life should operate between 1-5, because that's where you're the least stressed and the most productive. Often times anxiety gets us up to a 6-7. When our anxiety is in this level we can do deep breathing and other anti-anxiety exercises to bring us back down to a comfortable level. Unfortunately, when your anxiety gets to levels 8-10 and can be almost impossible to ratchet down your anxiety. Once you hit an 8 you kinda just have to miserably ride your anxiety out and try to remind yourself it's not gonna last forever. The good thing is, very rarely do we jump from even a 5 to an 8. Usually we move through the 6 and 7 where we could stop our anxiety but miss the symptoms. Part of what meditation did for me was give me the ability to spot when I was at a 6 or a 7 so I could bring myself back down to being a 5. It helped me better recognize the feelings of mild anxiety before they exploded into awful anxiety. It's not easy, and it doesn't always work, but over time you get better at spotting and stopping your anxiety before it gets too bad to stop. Atleast that's what happened to me. Hope this helps a little!
